title: Trump Says US May Take Stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic
summary:
President Donald Trump said in a TIME interview that he might take US government equity stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic, while rejecting nationalization of the AI companies. Asked about taking 10% stakes modeled on the government's Intel deal, he replied: “I might. Maybe I could do that.”

Trump said the Intel stake had made the government about $60 billion. OpenAI reportedly offered Washington a 5% stake in July, while Anthropic and the administration have denied discussing a stake in that company.

Asked what guardrails would apply if leading AI labs did bad things, Trump said: “I have a DOJ, I have an FBI.” AI researcher Gary Marcus challenged the prospect of government ownership, writing: “no way will this government properly police companies that it has a 10% equity stake in.”

🚨BREAKING: Trump just laid out his approach to frontier SI in a new TIME interview.

He called SI safety fears “phony threats” and said he is “not going to kill a thing” because of them.

TIME then asked whether that criticism included Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who had just spent 2½ hours at dinner with Trump the night before.

Trump: “Well, I don't know until last night. Yeah, yeah, but it could be. I mean, I don't know.”

He then called both Dario and Sam Altman “smart” and said the industry is dealing with “a very high level of IQ.”

Asked what his guardrail is if the top AI labs “do bad things”:

“I have a DOJ, I have an FBI.”

Trump rejected nationalizing frontier labs, but when TIME asked why the U.S. shouldn't take stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic like it did with Intel, he said:

“I might. Maybe I could do that.”

He also defended the data-center buildout, saying if America doesn't build them, they'll be built elsewhere, and added: “I don't want China to have all these data centers.”

🚨🇺🇸🇨🇳 Trump is making his AI strategy abundantly clear: America will NOT regulate itself out of the race.

After meeting with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Trump warned him that regulation could potentially “put you out of business.”

He said AI companies need to act responsibly themselves, emphasizing the U.S. is ahead of the rest of the world and attracting TRILLIONS in investment.

Trump’s calculation: AI carries serious risks, but losing America’s technological lead is even riskier...

Source: TIME / Writer: Samuel
